root.unit_estimated: Individual chick at day 14, with treatment assigned at the rearing-brood level and a random intercept for rearing nest
root.why: The fitted coefficient for net_rearing_manipulation directly estimates the within-frame effect of experimentally adding one sibling to the rearing brood on chick day-14 mass, in grams per additional sibling. Larger predictor values mean more sibling competition, matching the declared orientation. The reported estimate is -0.184 g per sibling (SE 0.015) on the linear model’s native outcome scale, using manipulated broods and the stated covariate adjustment and exclusions.

b2fc6827-2.unit_estimated: -0.0812 g per additional sibling competitor (SE 0.0161; z = -5.04; p ≈ 4.7×10^-7), on the linear mixed-model outcome scale
b2fc6827-2.why: The fitted analysis directly targets the declared estimand within frame: day-14 nestling mass regressed on d14_rear_nest_brood_size, constructed as the realized number of sibling competitors in the chick's rearing nest. Orientation is as_declared because larger values mean more competitors. Model: statsmodels MixedLM fitted by ML, with fixed effects for rear_nest_CS, rear_nest_LD, and year (2001–2003), plus a rearing-nest random intercept. Complete cases included 3,668 chicks from all 446 rearing broods; 52 observations missing lay date were excluded, and chick sex was not included because of substantial missingness. The estimate is therefore an adjusted change in day-14 mass per additional as-coded sibling competitor.

d8bb78fd-3.unit_estimated: −0.170 g of day-14 nestling mass per additional sibling added (cluster-robust SE 0.0146 g; t(316)=−11.68, p≈1.9×10^−26; n=2,698 chicks, 317 rearing broods)
d8bb78fd-3.why: This directly estimates the declared within-frame effect of sibling competition on nestling growth. Predictor: net_rearing_manipulation, constructed as the signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (positive=enlarged, negative=reduced); orientation: as_declared because larger values mean more siblings/competition. Chick-level OLS modeled day-14 mass in grams as a function of net_rearing_manipulation, rear_nest_CS, rear_nest_LD, and year fixed effects (2001 base). The sample retained complete cases from manipulated broods only (rear_nest_trt 5 or 6), excluding unmanipulated treatment 7 and 85 chicks missing the manipulation field. Sandwich SEs were clustered by rear_nest_breed_ID with correction G/(G−1)·(n−1)/(n−k), and inference used t with G−1=316 df.
